idiom_name: Rails routes -> controller action -> implicit ActionView render
implementation_notes: Rails is this pattern with the dispatcher declared in config/routes.rb: get "/orders/:id" => "orders#show" maps to OrdersController#show, the action is the worker (it loads the model through ActiveRecord and assigns instance variables), and Rails performs the implicit render of app/views/orders/show.html.erb unless the action calls render/redirect_to explicitly; ActionView helpers and partials are the view-helper slot, before_action filters and Rack middleware hold auth and logging. What replaces the classic structure is ActionDispatch routing plus ActionView implicit rendering; an explicit command/dispatcher module is justified only outside Rails (Sinatra or a bare Rack stack) or when actions must be resolved from data.
code_sketch:
class OrdersController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_user!            # front-controller work, per request

  def show
    @order = Order.includes(:lines).find(params[:id])   # worker services the request
    # Rails renders app/views/orders/show.html.erb with @order (implicit render)
  end
end
pitfalls: Instance variables are the model contract: a renamed ivar renders nil in the view without raising, so locals or a presenter make the contract checkable.
Associations read lazily in the view trigger queries during rendering (N+1); load them in the action with includes/preload.
Render twice, or render where an implicit render has already been decided, raises AbstractController::DoubleRenderError - redirect and return instead.
